Review accepted 3B across text sizes

This is the accepted unfolded screen only: soft neutral current-track container, bold current title, tonal Open, and transport 1B. For Camellia in the measured 414dp pane, the mode selector uses the first fitting connected arrangement in the one-row, 2×2, four-row sequence.

Every Android preset · 85% to 200%

What changed and what stayed fixed

  1. Direct target evidence: the installed SettingsGoogle.apk exposes exactly 85%, 100%, 115%, 130%, 150%, 180%, and 200%. The earlier 50% and 75% shell-injected states are excluded.
  2. Dynamic mode label: the third option names the active subdirectory. Its one-row content width is capped by Shuffle Camellia; longer names middle-ellipsize the subdirectory only while accessibility retains the full name.
  3. Adaptive row count: on this measured pane, complete labels try one connected row with variable-width content-sized cells, then a connected 2×2 block, then four connected vertical rows. No state scrolls horizontally.
  4. Accepted 3B: every capture retains the T3 current row, O2 tonal Open, centered transport, 24% seek position, outlined Previous and Next, and filled Pause.
  5. Native evidence: every image is an opaque 2076 × 2152px Compose capture of the 852 × 883dp unfolded Pixel 9 Pro Fold with Android system bars and live insets.

Observed wrapping

85% and 100% use one content-sized row. 115%, 130%, and 150% use 2×2. 180% and 200% use four rows.

Padding behavior

The one-row branch sizes each cell to its content and tries 12dp horizontal padding, then 6dp. The later branches add rows only when that fails. Targets remain at least 48dp.

Assistive technology boundary

Native semantics expose four radio options and the current-track description. Production assistive technology must still verify one mutually exclusive group announcement.

Priority: one row > two rows > four rows. Content-sized cells let Camellia remain on one row at 85% and 100%. Two rows ranks above four because it preserves deck space; four rows is the fallback that keeps every label complete. These are states of one adaptive design, not competing styles.

Exact accepted screen at every Android text preset

85% · content-sized one row

Smallest Android preset

Variable-width cells fit every complete label with Material's 12dp content padding.

Pros
  • One row preserves maximum deck height.
  • The complete Camellia label remains visible.
Cons
  • Cell widths differ because each follows its content.
100% · content-sized one row

Default Android scale

Compact 6dp content padding retains one line without clipping or horizontal scrolling.

Pros
  • One row preserves deck height at Android's default scale.
  • The complete current-subdirectory label remains visible.
Cons
  • Horizontal content padding falls from 12dp to 6dp.
115% · connected 2×2

First two-row preset

The content-sized one-row attempts no longer fit, so every label moves to connected 2×2.

Pros
  • All mode labels remain complete.
  • Track and folder text grows without changing row count.
Cons
  • Less list content fits than at 100%.
130% · connected 2×2

Intermediate enlarged preset

The connected block remains two rows with compact content padding.

Pros
  • Two rows preserve more deck height than the vertical fallback.
  • Every target remains connected and fully labeled.
Cons
  • Visible list density continues to decrease.
150% · connected 2×2

Largest two-row preset

Compact content padding keeps two segments per row without clipping.

Pros
  • 2×2 preserves deck height while retaining complete labels.
  • All four mode targets remain connected.
Cons
  • Less folder and track content fits in each pane.
180% · four rows

First vertical preset

Shuffle Camellia no longer fits a half-width segment, so each mode gets one row.

Pros
  • Every visible label remains complete.
  • The connected stack clears the navigation inset after deck scrolling.
Cons
  • Four rows consume more deck height than 2×2.
  • The evidence is a scrolled state.
200% · four rows

Largest Android preset

The vertical fallback preserves all four labels at Android's maximum setting.

Pros
  • Every mode label remains complete at the largest scale.
  • The full control clears the navigation inset after deck scrolling.
Cons
  • Four rows use the most deck height.
  • The evidence is a scrolled state.
